title: Ada and the Ghost
premise: Sebastian Okonkwo, a disgraced intelligence analyst scraping by on deniable freelance work, receives calls from a burner phone that shouldn't exist — the voice belongs to Ada Voss, his former handler who died eighteen months ago. Ada is alive, buried inside a private intelligence syndicate that manipulates markets through manufactured crises, and she needs Sebastian to extract her defector, a quant named Ilse Brandt, before Frankfurt opens and the syndicate's engineered collapse goes live. As Sebastian unravels who faked Ada's death and why, he discovers he himself was the syndicate's original test subject — his career destruction was their proof of concept. In the end, Sebastian gets Ilse out but lets the crash partially happen to expose the syndicate publicly, choosing justice outside the law over the clean win, while Ada walks away rather than return to a world that erased her once already.
about_author: August Galloway is the pen name of a former financial-crimes investigator who spent a decade inside compliance departments watching money move in ways no one wanted explained. Galloway writes thrillers about people the system discards and the quiet violence of institutions protecting themselves.

chapters.title: The Number That Calls Back
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Broke and blacklisted after three agency exits, Sebastian takes a low-grade surveillance job in London. A burner phone arrives in his mail slot with no sender; when it rings, the voice is Ada Voss — his old handler, officially dead. The emotional beat: disbelief curdling into hunger, because Ada offers the one thing he can't buy back: relevance.

chapters.title: Dead Handlers Tell No Tales
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Ada gives him a dead-drop protocol and a warning: verify everything, trust nothing she says directly. He digs into her death record and finds it too clean — a car fire, closed casket, a coroner who has since emigrated. Emotional beat: grief reawakening as suspicion; he wants her alive more than he wants the truth.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, with an intercut of Ilse Brandt's encrypted diary entries. Sebastian surveils Ilse, a syndicate quant planning defection with a drive full of trade algorithms keyed to staged geopolitical events. He realizes the 'defector' may be bait dangled to flush out whoever Ada turned. Emotional beat: professional cold war — every instinct says walk away, every scar says stay.

chapters.title: What They Did to Okonkwo
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian in flashback-heavy chapters as he traces the pattern of his own downfall: three agencies, three identical smear campaigns, one shell company funding all of them. The syndicate didn't recruit analysts — it manufactured unemployable ones and harvested them. Emotional beat: rage reframed as clarity; his ruin had an author.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Countdown
chapters.summary: POV alternating Sebastian and Ilse. With four days until markets open, Ada lays out the extraction: Ilse must be pulled from a syndicate safehouse during a scheduled security rotation. Sebastian tests Ada's intel against his own sources and finds one detail that doesn't fit — the rotation schedule is public knowledge. Emotional beat: dread; either Ada is compromised or Ada is the trap.

chapters.title: The Man Who Burned Me
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. He confronts Callum Reeve, the mid-level syndicate operator who signed off on his original blacklisting, in a Berlin hotel bar. Reeve, terrified, confirms the syndicate's structure and reveals there's a second burner phone — someone else is also talking to 'Ada.' Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of realizing you're one thread in someone else's web.

chapters.title: Two Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian finds the other phone's owner: a young analyst named Tomas, already dead, his extraction attempt failed two weeks ago. Comparing Tomas's notes with his own instructions, Sebastian sees the divergence point — Ada fed each of them half a plan. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into resolve; if Ada is playing him, he'll play the game better.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian and Ilse. The safehouse operation goes loud: Sebastian extracts Ilse through Frankfurt's transit tunnels while syndicate hunters close in, using the mismatched halves of both plans as misdirection. Ilse reveals the final piece — the crash isn't just profit, it's cover for a hostile takeover of a defense contractor. Emotional beat: adrenaline laced with moral nausea; saving her may still serve the machine.

chapters.title: The Price of Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Cornered at dawn, Ada finally appears in person and confesses: she let herself be 'killed' to infiltrate the syndicate, and she used Sebastian because his ruin made him invisible and expendable. She offers him the choice — stop the crash entirely and the syndicate buries everything, or let it burn and use the chaos to detonate the evidence publicly. Emotional beat: the climax of theme — justice that costs innocent people their savings.

chapters.title: Open
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian, closing with Ilse's testimony framing. Sebastian chooses the burn: the crash happens, brutal and partial, but the evidence floods regulators, journalists, and one relentless prosecutor simultaneously. The syndicate fractures; Reeve cooperates; Ada vanishes, leaving only the burner phone, now silent. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging — Sebastian, still ruined, finally owns the man they made him, and finds that enough.
